name: Coverage for Seniors Program
description: Premium-free prescription drug coverage for Alberta seniors aged 65+. Covers medications listed on the Alberta Drug Benefit List, diabetes supplies, and ambulance services. No premiums required. Co-payment is 30% of prescription cost to a maximum of $35 per prescription (as of April 2026). Coverage is automatically added to your AHCIP account when you turn 65.
hours_of_operation: Alberta Supports Contact Centre: Monday to Friday, 7:15 AM - 8:00 PM
eligibility: Automatic for all Alberta residents aged 65+ with active Alberta Health Care Insurance Plan (AHCIP) coverage. No income test. Must have age validated with AHCIP.
process_steps: Coverage is automatically added to your AHCIP account on the first of the month following your 65th birthday
No application or enrollment required
Present your Alberta health care card at the pharmacy when filling prescriptions
Pay the co-payment amount (30% to a max of $35 per prescription)
required_docs: Active Alberta Health Care Insurance Plan (AHCIP) card
Age validation on file with AHCIP
wait_times: Automatic — coverage begins the month after turning 65

name: Dental and Optical Assistance for Seniors
description: Income-tested dental and optical coverage for Alberta seniors aged 65+. Dental coverage provides up to $5,000 every 5 years for basic dental services (extractions, fillings, dentures, x-rays, cleanings). Optical coverage provides up to $230 every 3 years toward prescription eyeglasses. Eligibility is based on the previous year's total income as reported to CRA.
hours_of_operation: Alberta Supports Contact Centre: Monday to Friday, 7:15 AM - 8:00 PM
eligibility: Must be 65+ years old, lived in Alberta for at least 3 months, Canadian citizen or permanent resident, and have income within program thresholds. Must have an active file with the Alberta Seniors Benefit program. Income determined from previous year's CRA tax return.
process_steps: Ensure you have filed your income tax with CRA for the previous year
Apply through Alberta Supports Contact Centre or online
Income eligibility is verified against CRA records
If approved, receive a health benefits card listing eligible family members
Present card to dental provider or optician when receiving services
required_docs: Proof of age (65+)
Proof of Alberta residency (minimum 3 months)
Canadian citizenship or permanent residency documentation
Previous year's income tax filing with CRA (used for income verification)
wait_times: Eligibility determined for each benefit year (July 1 to June 30) based on previous year's income

name: Alberta Aids to Daily Living (AADL)
description: Provincial program providing funding for basic medical equipment and supplies for Albertans with long-term disabilities, chronic illness, or terminal illness. Covers wheelchairs, walkers, respiratory equipment, prosthetics, orthotics, ostomy supplies, catheters, incontinence products, hearing aids, and more. Clients pay 25% cost-share to a maximum of $500/year per individual or family. Low-income Albertans and income assistance recipients are exempt from cost-sharing.
hours_of_operation: HealthLink 811 available 24/7 for referrals; AADL authorizer appointments during business hours
eligibility: Alberta residents of any age with a long-term disability (minimum 6 months), chronic illness, or terminal illness who need medical equipment to maintain independence. Must be clinically assessed by an AADL-approved authorizer (registered nurse, occupational therapist, physiotherapist, etc.).
process_steps: Contact your local hospital, health care centre, or call HealthLink 811 to find an AADL authorizer
Get clinically assessed by an AADL-approved health care provider (authorizer)
Authorizer determines program eligibility and identifies appropriate products
Purchase approved equipment from an AADL-approved vendor (home health care stores, pharmacies, etc.)
Pay the 25% cost-share (up to $500/year max) unless exempt due to low income
required_docs: Active Alberta Health Care Insurance Plan (AHCIP) registration
Clinical assessment from an AADL-approved authorizer
Proof of low income or income assistance (if applying for cost-share exemption)
wait_times: Varies by location — depends on availability of AADL authorizers and equipment vendors in your area

name: Alberta Blue Cross Non-Group Coverage
description: Government-sponsored supplementary health benefits plan for Albertans under 65 who don't have employer or private coverage. Administered by Alberta Blue Cross on behalf of the Alberta government. Covers prescription drugs (from Alberta Drug Benefit List), dental, optical, ambulance, diabetic supplies, and clinical psychological services. Monthly premium required, with a Premium Subsidy Program available for lower-income Albertans. Prescription co-payment is 30% to a maximum of $35 (as of April 2026). $50 annual deductible on non-drug benefits.
hours_of_operation: Alberta Blue Cross: Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM - 5:00 PM; Online enrollment available 24/7
eligibility: All Alberta residents under 65 years of age registered under the Alberta Health Care Insurance Plan (AHCIP), and their dependants. No medical questions required to enroll. Available to those without employer or private health coverage.
process_steps: Confirm you have active AHCIP registration and are under 65
Complete the Non-Group Coverage application form (available online at alberta.ca or by calling Alberta Blue Cross)
Choose single or family coverage
Submit application to Alberta Blue Cross
If eligible for Premium Subsidy, apply separately to reduce monthly premium
Pay monthly premiums to maintain coverage
required_docs: Alberta Health Care Insurance Plan (AHCIP) card/number
Personal identification
For Premium Subsidy: proof of income (previous year's Notice of Assessment)
wait_times: Coverage typically begins the first of the month after application is processed

name: AISH Health Benefits
description: Comprehensive health benefits for AISH (Assured Income for the Severely Handicapped) recipients and their families. Covers prescription drugs (from Alberta Drug Benefit List plus some OTC medications and nutritional products), basic dental (extractions, fillings, dentures, x-rays, cleanings), optical (one eye exam every 2 years, one pair of glasses every 2 years for adults, yearly for children), diabetic supplies (test strips, insulin needles, infusion sets), and ambulance services. No premiums or co-payments.
hours_of_operation: Alberta Supports Contact Centre: Monday to Friday, 7:15 AM - 8:00 PM
eligibility: Must be an approved AISH recipient. AISH eligibility requires: age 18+, Alberta resident, Canadian citizen or permanent resident, have a severe and permanent disability that substantially limits ability to earn a living, and meet financial eligibility criteria. Coverage extends to cohabiting partner and dependent children.
process_steps: Apply for and be approved for AISH benefits through Alberta Supports
Receive your AISH Health Benefits Card in the mail listing all eligible family members
Present the health benefits card to your pharmacist, dentist, optician, or ambulance provider each time you receive services
If a drug or service is not covered, speak with your AISH worker about the Health Benefits Exception process
required_docs: AISH application and approval
Medical documentation of severe and permanent disability
Financial eligibility documentation
AISH Health Benefits Card (once approved)
wait_times: Health benefits begin once AISH application is approved (AISH processing can take several months)

name: Palliative Coverage Program
description: Provincial drug coverage program for Albertans in the end stage of a terminal illness who choose to remain at home or in a hospice. Covers prescription medications, specific laxatives, and hydration therapy solutions listed in the Alberta Drug Benefit List or the Palliative Care Drug Benefit Supplement. No co-payment required for eligible prescriptions (as of March 2020). Ensures dying Albertans can access needed medications without financial barriers.
address: Alberta Health, Attn: Alberta Palliative Coverage Program, PO Box 1360, Station Main, Edmonton, AB T5J 2N3
hours_of_operation: Alberta Supports Contact Centre: Monday to Friday, 7:15 AM - 8:00 PM
eligibility: Must be registered with AHCIP, diagnosed by a physician or nurse practitioner as being in the end stage of a terminal illness, have made a voluntary informed decision with a focus on palliation (not curative treatment), and remain at home or in a hospice (not in a facility that provides publicly funded drugs). Not available to residents of facilities that already provide publicly funded drugs, diabetes supplies, and ambulance services.
process_steps: Physician or nurse practitioner diagnoses patient as end-stage terminal illness
Patient (or guardian) and physician/nurse practitioner complete and sign the Palliative Coverage Program application form
Mail or fax completed form to Alberta Health Palliative Coverage Program in Edmonton
Receive written notification from Alberta Health regarding acceptance into the program
Once accepted, present AHCIP card at pharmacy for no-cost palliative prescriptions
required_docs: Completed Palliative Coverage Program application form (signed by both patient/guardian and physician/nurse practitioner)
Active Alberta Health Care Insurance Plan (AHCIP) registration
wait_times: Written notification sent after application is processed; typically within a few weeks

name: Non-Insured Health Benefits (NIHB)
description: Federal program providing registered First Nations and recognized Inuit with coverage for medically necessary health benefits not covered by provincial, territorial, or private insurance. Covers prescription drugs and OTC medications, dental care (no client co-payment), vision care (eye exams and glasses), medical supplies and equipment, mental health counselling, and medical transportation to access health services not available in the community of residence. Providers generally bill NIHB directly so clients pay nothing out of pocket.
hours_of_operation: Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM - 5:00 PM (Alberta regional office)
eligibility: Registered First Nations with a valid Indian Act registration number (status/treaty card) or recognized Inuit with an N-number issued by NIHB. Coverage is only for eligible goods and services obtained in Canada. Benefits are supplementary to provincial health insurance and any private insurance coverage.
process_steps: Confirm your registration status (First Nations registration number from status/treaty card, or Inuit N-number)
Present your client identification (status card or NIHB ID) to your health care provider
Provider verifies eligibility and bills NIHB directly in most cases
No upfront payment required for most services — provider submits claim to NIHB
Some services may require prior approval from NIHB before receiving treatment
required_docs: Indian Act registration number (status/treaty card) or Certificate of Indian Status letter, OR
Inuit N-number (mailed to recognized Inuit clients)
Provincial health care card
wait_times: Immediate access for most services once registered; some services require prior approval

name: Interim Federal Health Program (IFHP)
description: Federal program providing temporary health coverage to refugees, refugee claimants, and other protected persons in Canada who are not yet eligible for provincial health insurance. Covers basic health care (doctor visits, hospital care — no co-payment), supplemental benefits (dental, vision, counselling, assistive devices), and prescription drugs. As of May 2026, co-payments apply to supplemental services: $4 per prescription, 30% for dental/vision/counselling. Basic health care remains fully covered with no co-payment.
hours_of_operation: IRCC Call Centre: Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM - 4:00 PM
eligibility: Refugee claimants awaiting a decision, protected persons, resettled refugees not yet eligible for provincial health insurance, and those with rejected claims eligible for PRRA. In most cases, eligibility is based on immigration status and coverage is activated automatically. Some may need to apply for an IFHP eligibility certificate.
process_steps: In most cases, IFHP coverage is activated automatically based on your immigration status — no application needed
If you need an eligibility certificate, complete and submit the IFHP application form (Guide 5568)
Receive your IFHP certificate of eligibility
Present your IFHP document to health care providers when seeking treatment
Provider bills IFHP directly; you pay applicable co-payments for supplemental services (as of May 2026)
required_docs: Immigration or refugee claim documentation
IFHP eligibility certificate (if not automatically enrolled)
For manual application: completed Guide 5568 form
wait_times: Coverage typically begins automatically with your refugee claim; basic coverage lasts until you qualify for provincial health insurance

name: Residential Access Modification Program (RAMP)
description: Provincial grant program providing up to $12,000 per person per benefit year (April 1 to March 31) to help lower-income Albertans with mobility challenges modify their homes. Covers modifications like wheelchair ramps, widened doorways, accessible bathrooms, stair lifts, and other changes that help wheelchair or walker users enter and move around their homes. Applications prioritized for those awaiting hospital discharge or in palliative care.
address: RAMP, Assisted Living and Social Services, PO Box 808, Edmonton Main, Edmonton, AB T5J 2L4
hours_of_operation: Alberta Supports Contact Centre: Monday to Friday, 7:15 AM - 8:00 PM
eligibility: Low-income Albertans of any age who use a wheelchair, seniors (65+) who use a 4-wheel walker on an ongoing basis, or people living with a progressive neuro-degenerative disease. Must meet income thresholds.
process_steps: Obtain an occupational therapy (OT) assessment confirming mobility challenges and home modification needs
Get written renovation quotes from contractors for required modifications
Complete the RAMP application form
Submit application with OT assessment, renovation quotes, and income documentation to RAMP office in Edmonton
Receive a funding decision letter within 30 days of applying
If approved, complete the home modifications
Submit receipts for reimbursement
required_docs: Completed RAMP application form
Occupational therapy assessment documenting mobility needs
Written renovation quotes or estimates from contractors
Proof of income (income verification documentation)
Proof of Alberta residency
wait_times: Funding decision within 30 days of application; prioritized for hospital discharge or palliative care situations

name: Seniors Home Adaptation and Repair Program (SHARP)
description: Provincial program helping Alberta seniors maintain their homes and independence through low-interest home equity loans of up to $40,000, or grants for those who don't qualify for a loan. Covers essential repairs, adaptations, and renovations to a senior's primary residence. Loan requires minimum 25% home equity. Grants available for very low-income seniors (single: $34,770/year or less; couple: $56,820/year or less) who lack sufficient equity. A loan estimator is available online.
address: SHARP, PO Box 1050, STN Main, Edmonton, AB T5J 2M1
hours_of_operation: Alberta Supports Contact Centre: Monday to Friday, 7:15 AM - 8:00 PM
eligibility: For loans: Alberta seniors (65+) or senior couples with total annual income of $75,000 or less and minimum 25% home equity in primary residence. For grants: single seniors with annual income of $34,770 or less, or senior couples with combined annual income of $56,820 or less, who are not eligible for a loan (e.g., insufficient equity or not a fee simple homeowner).
process_steps: Determine if you qualify for a loan or grant using the online SHARP loan estimator
Get written cost estimates or receipts for planned repairs/renovations
Complete and sign the SHARP Loan Application and Agreement form
Include all required supporting documents (property tax assessment, estimates/receipts)
Mail or fax application to SHARP office in Edmonton
Receive a decision on your application
Complete repairs and provide documentation as required
required_docs: Completed SHARP Loan Application and Agreement form
Property tax assessment or bill
Written cost estimates or receipts for planned work
Proof of income
Proof of home ownership and equity
wait_times: Processing time varies; contact Alberta Supports for current timelines

name: Home Accessibility Tax Credit (HATC)
description: Federal non-refundable tax credit for home accessibility renovations. Claim up to $20,000 in eligible expenses per year for renovations that improve accessibility or reduce risk of harm. Provides a 15% tax credit worth up to $3,000. Eligible expenses include professional installation of wheelchair ramps, walk-in bathtubs, grab bars, widened doorways, lowered countertops, hands-free faucets, and other permanent accessibility improvements. Can be claimed by the qualifying individual, their spouse, or a supporting family member.
hours_of_operation: CRA general inquiries: Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM - 8:00 PM local time
eligibility: Qualifying individuals must be 65+ years old OR eligible for the Disability Tax Credit (DTC). Renovations must be to the individual's principal residence. Expenses must be for work done to allow the person to gain access to the dwelling, be mobile within it, or reduce the risk of harm. Work must be performed by a professional and result in permanent changes to the home.
process_steps: Determine if you or a family member qualifies (65+ or DTC eligible)
Complete eligible accessibility renovations at your principal residence using professional contractors
Keep all receipts for materials and labour
Claim expenses on Line 31285 of your annual income tax return
Tax credit is calculated at 15% of eligible expenses up to $20,000
required_docs: Receipts for all renovation expenses (materials and labour)
Disability Tax Credit certificate (Form T2201) if claiming based on disability
Proof of age if claiming as a senior
Completed income tax return with Line 31285
wait_times: Credit applied when annual tax return is assessed (typically February to June)

name: Easter Seals AccessABILITIES Home Automation Program
description: Charitable program providing Albertans living with a disability access to smart home technology to increase independence. Available equipment includes smart speakers, smart displays, smart plugs, smart lighting, smart thermostats, smart locks, and video doorbells. Funding is based on both physical need (documented disability) and financial need. Helps people with mobility, sensory, neurological, or other disabilities control their home environment with voice commands or minimal physical effort.
address: 101, 340 Midpark Way SE, Calgary, AB T2X 1P1
eligibility: Must be 18+ years old, reside in Alberta, be a Canadian citizen or permanent resident, and have a chronic developmental, physical, sensory, mental, or neurological condition or impairment. Must demonstrate both physical need for the equipment and financial need for assistance.
process_steps: Complete the AccessABILITIES application form (available online at easterseals.ab.ca)
Provide supporting documentation of disability (doctor's prescription, OT/PT assessment, or letter from appropriate professional)
Complete the financial need section of the application
Submit application and wait for a caseworker to review
Caseworker contacts you to discuss needs and determine eligibility
If approved, receive and install smart home equipment
required_docs: Completed AccessABILITIES application form
Doctor's prescription, occupational/physical therapist assessment, or professional letter of support documenting disability
Financial information demonstrating need for funding assistance
Proof of Alberta residency
Proof of Canadian citizenship or permanent residency
wait_times: Varies based on application volume and available funding; contact Easter Seals for current timelines

name: Alberta Disability Assistance Program (ADAP)
description: New provincial program launching July 1, 2026, providing income support and health benefits for Albertans with severe disabilities who are able to work. Monthly core benefit of up to $1,740 with the highest employment income exemption in Canada, allowing recipients to earn more from working while continuing to receive benefits. Health benefits will continue regardless of employment income. Designed to close the gap between AISH (for those unable to work) and other supports. All AISH clients will be transitioned to ADAP on July 1, 2026, with a transition benefit ensuring existing AISH benefit rates are maintained.
hours_of_operation: Alberta Supports Contact Centre: Monday to Friday, 7:15 AM - 8:00 PM
eligibility: Albertans with a severe disability that significantly restricts (but does not prevent) employment. Must be assessed for both ADAP and AISH to determine best fit. Specific eligibility criteria and benefit rates will be finalized in regulations expected Spring 2026. Existing AISH clients will be automatically transitioned.
process_steps: Starting July 1, 2026: new disability income assistance applicants will be assessed for both ADAP and AISH
Existing AISH clients: automatic transition to ADAP on July 1, 2026 (no application needed)
New applicants: apply through Alberta Supports
Undergo medical eligibility assessment to determine if disability significantly restricts (ADAP) or prevents (AISH) employment
If approved, receive monthly core benefit and health benefits
Health benefits continue regardless of employment income level
required_docs: Medical documentation of severe disability
Employment and income information
Alberta residency documentation
Specific documentation requirements to be finalized in Spring 2026 regulations
wait_times: Program launches July 1, 2026; processing times to be determined. Existing AISH clients transition automatically.
